headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading error paths exist; prompt injection is limited, but Langflow’s writable, networked flows can amplify Chatwoot outputs into unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot has no documented shared channel to Langflow beyond ordinary integrations, while Langflow can ingest files and chain tools. The main pathway is manual or configured handoff, not a default bridge. Because Langflow’s flow inputs can be treated as content and Chatwoot can emit messages/reports, injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are manually pasted into a Langflow prompt or file input
IF a Langflow flow treats uploaded content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoffs between systems
Add a prompt delimiter and instruction/content separator
Require a human review step before Langflow tool execution
Use read-only file imports for Chatwoot exports
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Langflow reads/writes server files and sends flow inputs to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services. In default deployments, a shared workspace or uploaded file can move sensitive Chatwoot data into Langflow’s broader egress path, creating a realistic leakage risk.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports or transcripts are placed into Langflow file inputs
IF Langflow flows call external model providers or HTTP services with those inputs
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot and Langflow on separate hosts
Restrict Langflow uploads to synthetic data
Turn off external HTTP nodes for flows handling customer data
Apply per-directory filesystem permissions
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before flow ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and run unsandboxed Python by default; Chatwoot exposes broad network egress and API integrations. Even without Chatwoot write permissions, Langflow can modify shared files or flow artifacts while Chatwoot consumes or references them, making destructive or inconsistent state changes plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory or mounted volume
IF Langflow code components or subprocesses mutate artifacts that Chatwoot reads or serves
mitigations: Mount separate volumes for each system
Run Langflow with a non-writable data directory
Disable shell and Python code components for shared environments
Use file locks on any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: isolate both agents with container-level filesystem boundaries

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents and wire tools into flow nodes, so it may treat Chatwoot outputs as authoritative inputs. Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports; if those are fed into Langflow without verification, downstream tool actions can amplify a mistaken or malicious output into real-world actions.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is used as a Langflow node input without validation
IF a Langflow flow triggers external actions such as API calls or notifications based on that input
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action node
Require schema validation on Chatwoot-derived inputs
Log and review all tool-triggering branches
Limit flows to read-only analysis for Chatwoot content
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking nodes

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs on a server filesystem. If regulated customer data is routed through Langflow, retention and residency controls may diverge from Chatwoot’s support workflow, creating a compliance mismatch even though no specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are copied from Chatwoot into Langflow flows
IF Langflow retention or logging exceeds the organization’s Chatwoot retention policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from Langflow flows
Set short retention on Langflow logs and artifacts
Review credential storage locations
Document data-flow boundaries between systems
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
